errors.evidence: The figure consists of two separate, side-by-side bar charts (one for "Deutschland" and one for the "EU"), not a single bar chart.

The description completely fails to mention that there are two separate charts, one for "Deutschland" (Germany) and one for the "EU". This is a critical omission that makes the subsequent data reporting nonsensical.
The description uses the term "Importvolumen" (import volume), but the y-axis is labeled with '%' and represents the percentage share of imports, not an absolute volume.
The color for the year 2022 is purple, not light blue ("hellblau").

errors.text_span: Die Importwerte für Aluminium betragen 2021 3,6 %, 2022 4,4 % und 2023 5,1 %. Die Importwerte für Kupfer belägen 2021 1,0 %, 2022 1,7 % und 2023 1,3 %. Die Importwerte für Nickel beliefen sich auf 2,2 % im Jahr 2021, 2,8 % im Jahr 2022 und 1,4 % im Jahr 2023.
errors.evidence: This entire section is incorrect. The description fails to distinguish between the Germany and EU charts and proceeds to list values that are completely mismatched with the materials and years. For example, for Aluminium, it gives 4.4% for 2022 (the actual values are 2.7% for Germany and 2.8% for the EU) and 5.1% for 2023 (actual values are 1.0% and 1.7%). The values listed appear to be taken almost randomly from different categories across both charts.

errors.text_span: Die Balken zeigen eine allgemeine Variation der Importvolumina für jeden Rohstoff im Zeitverlauf, wobei die höchsten Werte im Allgemeinen im Jahr 2022 und die niedrigsten im Jahr 2023 zu sehen sind.
errors.evidence: This sentence provides an interpretation of trends which is also an over-generalization. The claim that the highest values are generally in 2022 is only true for Copper; for Aluminium and Nickel, the highest values are in 2021.
